nodes.summary: There exist an integer $n \ge 1$ and a group $G$ such that $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$ but some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has infinite order. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 13.34 (I. D. Macdonald; V. D. Mazurov) in the negative, by results of G. S. Deryabina and P. A. Kozhevnikov from 1999 and of S. I. Adyan from 2000.
nodes.title: A commutator power identity need not make the derived subgroup periodic

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every group $G$ with $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$, every element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has finite order, that is, the derived subgroup of $G$ is periodic.
nodes.title: Derived subgroups under a commutator power identity (Kourovka 13.34)
